prompt: Segment the white-matter (FLAIR-hyperintense) MS lesions of patient01 of the open_ms_data cross-sectional dataset, producing a binary lesion mask in the FLAIR space of the co-registered resampled images.
reference: Expert multi-rater consensus lesion mask (three raters) shipped with the Ljubljana MS database, on the co-registered-resampled FLAIR grid the task hands out (voxel data as published; header taken from FLAIR, which the published mask misses by <= 0.4 mm).
threshold_basis: FIXED (published, dataset-specific): anchors are the LST-AI evaluation on `msljub` — the same Ljubljana 30-patient cohort and the same multi-rater consensus reference standard used here (Wiltgen et al. 2024, NeuroImage: Clinical 42:103611, doi:10.1016/j.nicl.2024.103611). full = LST-AI, the best published method on this dataset (Dice 0.74, lesion-wise F1 0.70); zero-credit line = LST-LGA, the weakest legitimate published tool on it (Dice 0.53, F1 0.33); SAMSEG (0.62/0.47) and nnU-Net (0.58/0.54) fall mid-band. Those anchors transfer only because the lesion-counting convention matches: the same >=10 % overlap rule for a detection and the same 3 mm3 minimum lesion size (`min_lesion_voxels` = 3), which here excludes 130 of 408 reference foci holding 0.5 % of the lesion volume. Dice is computed on the full masks. Volume-error band 15 %/50 % is the shared lesion-pack convention, not a published value. The individual rater masks are not public, so no inter-rater envelope can be derived from this subject; a single subject also gives no leave-one-out envelope. lesion-wise F1 carries Dice's weight because MS lesion burden is multifocal — detection, not only boundary overlap, is the clinical quantity.
reference_notes: consensus lesion volume 31.42 cm3, 408 foci (median 0.011 cm3, largest 4.93 cm3); 278 foci counted as lesion instances at min_lesion_voxels=3
references: Lesjak Z, Galimzianova A, Koren A, et al. A Novel Public MR Image Dataset of Multiple Sclerosis Patients With Lesion Segmentations Based on Multi-rater Consensus. Neuroinformatics 16:51-63, 2018. doi:10.1007/s12021-017-9348-7 (dataset and three-rater consensus reference standard; CC-BY).

Wiltgen T, McGinnis J, Schlaeger S, et al. LST-AI: A deep learning ensemble for accurate MS lesion segmentation. NeuroImage: Clinical 42:103611, 2024. doi:10.1016/j.nicl.2024.103611 (per-dataset Dice / lesion-wise F1 on msljub for LST-AI, LST-LPA, LST-LGA, SAMSEG and nnU-Net; source of the threshold anchors).
